_about: Condensed, plain-language statements of Indian statutory provisions relevant to commercial contract review. Each 'text' is an editorial summary, NOT a verbatim quotation of the bare Act; 'provision' gives the citation to check against the authoritative text on indiacode.nic.in. Indian legislative text is not subject to copyright (Copyright Act, 1957 s.52(1)(q)).

provisions.heading: What agreements are contracts
provisions.text: An agreement is a contract if it is made by the free consent of parties competent to contract, for a lawful consideration and with a lawful object, and is not expressly declared void. Certain contracts must also be in writing, registered or attested where other laws so require.

provisions.heading: What consideration and objects are lawful, and what not
provisions.text: The consideration or object of an agreement is unlawful if it is forbidden by law, would defeat the provisions of any law, is fraudulent, involves injury to person or property, or is regarded by the court as immoral or opposed to public policy. An agreement with an unlawful object or consideration is void.

provisions.heading: Agreement in restraint of trade, void
provisions.text: Every agreement by which anyone is restrained from exercising a lawful profession, trade or business of any kind is, to that extent, void. The only statutory exception is a restraint accepted by the seller of the goodwill of a business, within reasonable local limits, while a like business is carried on by the buyer. Indian courts generally do not enforce post-employment non-compete restrictions.

provisions.heading: Agreements in restraint of legal proceedings, void
provisions.text: An agreement that absolutely restricts a party from enforcing its rights through the ordinary tribunals, or that limits the time within which rights may be enforced to less than the statutory limitation period, is void to that extent. A clause that extinguishes a right or discharges a liability on expiry of a specified period is also void. Bona fide arbitration agreements are expressly saved.

provisions.heading: Compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract
provisions.text: On breach, the injured party is entitled to compensation for loss or damage that naturally arose in the usual course of things from the breach, or that the parties knew when contracting to be likely to result. Remote or indirect loss is not compensable. The claimant must also take reasonable steps to mitigate its loss.

provisions.heading: Compensation for breach of contract where penalty stipulated for
provisions.text: Where a sum is named in the contract as payable on breach, or the contract contains any other stipulation by way of penalty, the injured party is entitled to reasonable compensation not exceeding that sum, whether or not actual loss is proved. Courts relieve against amounts that are penal rather than a genuine pre-estimate of loss; this is often applied to liquidated damages and to high default-interest rates.

provisions.heading: Contract of indemnity defined
provisions.text: A contract of indemnity is one by which one party promises to save the other from loss caused to the other by the conduct of the promisor or of any other person. Indian statute defines indemnity narrowly around loss caused by human conduct; wider indemnities (including against loss from events) are given effect as ordinary contractual promises.

provisions.heading: Rights of indemnity-holder when sued
provisions.text: An indemnity-holder acting within the scope of its authority is entitled to recover from the indemnifier all damages, costs and sums paid under any compromise of a suit in respect of a matter covered by the indemnity, provided the holder acted prudently and with authority.

provisions.heading: Arbitration agreement
provisions.text: An arbitration agreement is an agreement to submit to arbitration present or future disputes arising out of a defined legal relationship. It must be in writing, which includes a signed document, an exchange of communications recording the agreement, or an exchange of pleadings in which its existence is alleged and not denied. A reference in a contract to a document containing an arbitration clause incorporates that clause if the reference makes it part of the contract.

provisions.heading: Appointment of arbitrators
provisions.text: Parties are free to agree a procedure for appointing the arbitral tribunal. Failing agreement or cooperation, a party may apply to the Supreme Court (international commercial arbitration) or the High Court (other cases), or their designated institution, to make the appointment. The court confines its examination to the existence of an arbitration agreement.

provisions.heading: Place of arbitration
provisions.text: The parties are free to agree on the place (seat) of arbitration. Failing agreement, the tribunal determines it having regard to the circumstances and the parties' convenience. The tribunal may meet at any place it considers appropriate for hearings or deliberations. The seat fixes which courts exercise supervisory jurisdiction over the arbitration.

provisions.heading: Rules applicable to substance of dispute
provisions.text: In an arbitration seated in India other than an international commercial arbitration, the tribunal decides the dispute according to the substantive law of India. In international commercial arbitration the tribunal applies the law designated by the parties. In all cases the tribunal decides in accordance with the contract terms and takes trade usages into account.

provisions.heading: Application for setting aside arbitral award
provisions.text: Recourse against a domestic award is limited to an application to set it aside on narrow grounds: incapacity, an invalid arbitration agreement, lack of proper notice, the award exceeding the scope of submission, improper composition of the tribunal, non-arbitrability, or conflict with the public policy of India (including fraud, or patent illegality for purely domestic awards). The application must generally be made within three months.

provisions.heading: Contracts not specifically enforceable
provisions.text: Certain contracts cannot be specifically enforced, including those where compensation in money is an adequate relief, contracts that run into minute or numerous details or depend on the personal qualifications of a party, contracts of a determinable nature, and contracts involving continuous duties the court cannot supervise. Following the 2018 amendment, specific performance is otherwise the norm rather than a discretionary exception.

provisions.heading: Injunction when refused
provisions.text: An injunction cannot be granted to restrain a person from prosecuting proceedings (except to prevent a multiplicity of proceedings), to restrain proceedings in a court not subordinate to that from which the injunction is sought, to prevent a breach of contract the performance of which could not be specifically enforced, or where the applicant has no personal interest in the matter.

provisions.heading: Unfair contract; power to declare terms void
provisions.text: An 'unfair contract' is one between a manufacturer or trader or service provider and a consumer that causes significant change in consumer rights, including by requiring excessive security deposits, imposing a disproportionate penalty for breach, refusing to accept early repayment, allowing unilateral termination without cause, permitting assignment to the consumer's detriment, or imposing unreasonable charges or conditions. The State Commission and National Commission may declare such terms null and void.

provisions.heading: Instruments executed in India to be stamped before or at execution
provisions.text: An instrument chargeable with duty and executed in India must be stamped before or at the time of execution. Stamp duty is a State subject, so the rate and mode (physical or e-stamp) depend on the State where the instrument is executed or the property is situated.

provisions.heading: Instruments not duly stamped inadmissible in evidence
provisions.text: An instrument that is not duly stamped cannot be admitted in evidence, acted upon, or registered, unless the deficient duty and a penalty are paid to have it validated. An unstamped or under-stamped arbitration agreement or contract can therefore stall enforcement until it is impounded and regularised.

provisions.heading: Documents of which registration is compulsory
provisions.text: Registration is compulsory for instruments that create, declare, assign, limit or extinguish any right, title or interest in immovable property worth one hundred rupees or more, and for leases of immovable property from year to year or for a term exceeding one year. An unregistered document that requires registration cannot affect the immovable property or be received as evidence of the transaction, though it may be used for limited collateral purposes.

provisions.heading: Validity of contracts formed through electronic means
provisions.text: Where a contract is formed by communication of proposals, acceptances and revocations in electronic form or by electronic records, the contract is not unenforceable merely because electronic means were used. This supports click-wrap and email execution, subject to the Stamp Act and any law requiring a specific form.

provisions.heading: Grounds for processing personal data
provisions.text: Personal data may be processed only for a lawful purpose for which the data principal has given consent, or for certain 'legitimate uses' specified in the Act. Processing must be tied to the stated purpose.

provisions.heading: Consent
provisions.text: Consent must be free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous, given by a clear affirmative action, and limited to the personal data necessary for the specified purpose. The data principal may withdraw consent at any time with consequences borne by the principal, and the request for consent must be accompanied by a plain-language notice.

provisions.heading: General obligations of Data Fiduciary
provisions.text: A data fiduciary is responsible for compliance even when processing is done by a data processor engaged under a valid contract. It must maintain accuracy, implement reasonable security safeguards, notify the Board and affected principals of a personal data breach, and erase personal data on withdrawal of consent or when the purpose is no longer served.
